config._note: Sim 4 greenfield: an understanding-only transfer test of the infill-chosen sensors against imaginary edge estates; not a planning or capacity study. One representative per edge stretch, with at least min_homes of downstream property headroom on every route, including relief pipes.
config._source: SA Water Sewerage Code Supplement Pt 1, cl 4.5.5 and Table 4.4 (Amdt Jun09): maximum allowable EP 1000/2500/4500 for DN150/225/300, equivalent properties 400/1000/1800.
config._property_limits: SA Water Supplement Table 4.4 limits apply only to reticulation sewers, DN150-300. Above DN300 (branch and trunk sewers, DN375+), there is no property limit; capacity is left to SWMM. Below DN150 use 400 x (D/0.150)^(8/3), a team scaling assumption. Other unlisted reticulation diameters scale from the nearest table DN at equal slope and roughness; within 5 mm of a listed DN use that entry. D is in metres.
config._assumptions: Estate sizes and the short edge connection are team assumptions. Every site's ceiling is the smaller of floored property headroom and the largest configured step; a path with no Table 4.4 cap uses that largest step. Retain every smaller configured step plus the ceiling.
config._edge: Open sector beside the manhole, using all gravity pipes held by Network sampled every 10 m and existing homes/connections; its middle must have 60 m clearance towards open land. Cluster sites sharing a non-null limiting pipe or lying within cluster_radius_m with bearings within cluster_angle_deg; keep the largest sector, then lowest manhole id.
config._estate_ii: Team assumption: add sewage only, exactly as Sim25Model greenfield growth does, with no extra infiltration for the estate's own new pipes. No public data gives estate pipe lengths or infiltration.

weather.label: Dry
weather.note: Sewage only, no infiltration: a genuinely dry day.

weather.label: Design wet
weather.note: Infiltration at the level that just meets the utility's own design rating for these pipes.

weather.label: Beyond design
weather.note: 1.7 times the design envelope: a wet day on a leaky network.

weather.label: Severe
weather.note: 2.4 times the design envelope: a heavy wet period.

data_notes: A greenfield estate joins a manhole on the network's edge, where open land lies beside it (an open sector of at least 120 degrees with no pipes or homes within 200 m, clear for 400 m along its middle); an estate in the middle of the built network would need a second sewer under existing streets.

This family is for understanding whether the infill-chosen sensors notice hypothetical growth at an edge connection. It is not a planning, serviceability or capacity study; geometric openness does not establish access, land availability or a feasible receiving invert.

Geometry uses every gravity pipe held by Network, including non-domain/statewide pipes if held, sampled every 10 m, and all retained homes and property connection points. It does not import extra surrounding GIS. The sector ignores points within 15 m; the 60 m clearance is checked along the ray from 60 m to its configured end, allowing the short connection beside the existing pipe.
outgoing_dn is a list of recorded diameters in mm, in outgoing pipe order; limiting_pipe_dn is also in mm. Pipe ids are published asset ids; pipe indices are Network indices.
At splits, every downstream route must have headroom. Shared upstream properties are counted once per pipe, including relief loops; no hydraulic flow split is assumed.

Limits are from SA Water Supplement Table 4.4 for reticulation sewers (DN150-300). Only pipes DN <= 300 constrain property headroom on each downstream path. Branch and trunk capacity (DN375+) is left to SWMM, with no property limit above DN300.
Below DN150 the limit scales from DN150; other unlisted reticulation diameters scale from the nearest Table 4.4 DN at equal slope and roughness. This is a team calculation.

Estate sizes, the short connection at the network edge and estate infiltration are team assumptions because no public data gives them. The estate adds sewage only, with no extra infiltration for its own new pipes, exactly as Sim25Model growth does. For paths without a reticulation constraint, the largest configured estate size caps the ladder only.
Table 4.4 limits apply to total EP on a pipe, expressed here as equivalent properties using the configured Table 4.4 property limits; they are not an allowance for new properties alone.

Boundary conversion is a team estimate: use Sim25's estimated/countable connections, not total boundary L/s divided by sewage per property. Boundary L/s includes both sewage and I&I, on the nominal Sim25 case basis.

Counts include unique upstream Pipe.dwellings, boundary properties at their joins and wet-well catchments transferred at pump discharges. Downstream checks follow pumps as well as gravity pipes. Hydraulic constraints are tested by the SWMM run stage.

Headroom is displayed to one decimal; integer steps use floor of unrounded headroom, capped at the largest configured step for every site. All smaller configured steps are retained. 'No table cap' means no Table 4.4 property limit above DN300, not unlimited hydraulic capacity.

Existing dwellings use 2.81 people per connection; new dwellings use 2.3, both at the same configured peaking factor (2 for these peak-hour cases). b1.5 multiplies boundary sewage AND boundary I&I by 1.5; it does not multiply existing in-domain sewage, in-domain I&I or estate sewage. Estates add no infiltration: a sewage-only control. Pumped estates use their smoothed peak-hour flow in the primary cases.

The _pumprate bracket uses max(estate peak-hour flow, 7.8540 L/s), from 1 m/s in the smallest published rising main DN100, only for sites flagged levels.pumped in simulation4/data/estates.js. Gravity estates are unchanged. This is steady depth while the pump runs, an upper bound, not a volume-preserving duty-cycle model.
Missing pumped flags are treated as gravity: none.

The _together case loads all representatives at once at 30, 80 and 150 homes each, capped individually. The _with_infill case loads every representative at 150 homes (or its ceiling) on top of the largest Sim4 infill step in each distinct containing region. Its baseline includes that same infill background, so rises isolate the additional estates.

Exclusion order: receives pumped or outside flow, not on the network's edge, unknown diameter, headroom below minimum, then same edge stretch. Clusters are connected components sharing a non-null limiting pipe or within the configured distance and bearing difference; the largest open sector wins, then the lowest manhole id. Counts are exclusive.
Remaining limits: no pump duty-cycle bursts; free outfall (no tailwater); steady peak hour only (no trough, diurnal or wet-weather timing); relief inlets as configured (published).
The gravity domain has 6 terminals, including pump wet wells and relief exits; all reachable downstream gravity paths are checked.
